extra_misconceptions.fact: Clostridium tetani spores thrive in rich garden soil and manure, entering the body through any dirty puncture or scratch.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Tetanus bacteria only live on rusty metal garden tools rather than in organic garden soil and compost.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Burning poison ivy vaporizes urushiol oil into the smoke, which can cause severe, life-threatening lung inflammation if inhaled.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Burning pulled poison ivy vines with yard waste safely destroys the allergenic plant oils on contact.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Pinching the attached venom sac forces more toxin into the skin; scrape the stinger sideways using a flat edge like a credit card.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Squeezing a honeybee venom sac with tweezers pulls the stinger out cleanly without injecting more venom.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Up to 80 percent of solar ultraviolet rays penetrate cloud cover, requiring broad-spectrum SPF 30 sunscreen and protective clothing.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cloudy overcast days block ultraviolet radiation enough that gardeners do not need sunscreen or wide-brimmed hats.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to leave a deep soil puncture wound unwashed even if the bleeding stops right away?
Which physical indicator distinguishes heat exhaustion from life-threatening heatstroke during summer weeding?
What happens to urushiol oil from poison ivy if you wipe your forehead with contaminated gardening gloves?
Under what condition does a routine bee or wasp sting in the garden require an immediate epinephrine injection?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sowing seeds too deeply exhausts their stored cotyledon energy before the shoot can reach sunlight at the soil surface.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Planting vegetable seeds twice as deep as the packet recommends anchors the emerging stem against heavy wind.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Shallow daily sprinkling keeps roots near the hot surface and wets foliage; deep, infrequent morning soaking promotes deep roots.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Watering garden beds lightly every afternoon with a mist nozzle builds deep, drought-tolerant root systems.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Disturbing the delicate taproot of carrots or radishes during transplanting causes forked, stunted, or malformed storage roots.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Root vegetables like carrots and radishes recover quickly when started in indoor cell trays and transplanted.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Excess nitrogen stimulates lush, leafy green foliage at the expense of flower buds and fruit set, which require phosphorus and potassium.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: High-nitrogen lawn fertilizer forces flowering annuals and fruiting tomatoes to produce maximum blossoms.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to indoor-grown vegetable seedlings if you transplant them into full sun without hardening them off?
Which physical indicator on a seedling root ball shows that a nursery transplant has become severely root-bound?
Where should a Scout position tall stake-supported crops like tomatoes so they do not shade low-growing flowers?
What measurement confirms that your garden soil has warmed enough to direct-sow warm-season vegetable seeds?

extra_misconceptions.fact: White potatoes are stem tubers rich in potassium and vitamin C, while sweet potatoes are storage roots packed with beta-carotene.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: White potatoes and sweet potatoes are both modified taproots that store identical amounts of beta-carotene.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Any seed-bearing structure that develops from the fertilized ovary of a flower, including cucumbers, peppers, and peas, is a fruit.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Botanical fruits must taste sweet and grow on woody trees or perennial bushes rather than annual garden vines.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Human enzymes cannot digest plant cellulose fiber, which instead adds bulk to aid digestion and regulate blood sugar absorption.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Dietary fiber in leafy greens and fruit skins provides a major source of digestible calories for human muscles.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Respiration rapidly converts the natural sugars in freshly picked sweet corn and peas into starchy carbohydrates unless chilled.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Harvested sweet corn and garden peas gain additional simple sugars as they sit on a warm kitchen counter for days.

extra_socratic_questions: Which botanical structure inside a ripened flower ovary classifies a tomato or squash as a fruit rather than a vegetable?
What happens to the water-soluble vitamin C content of broccoli or spinach when boiled in a large pot of water?
Why is it nutritionally beneficial to scrub rather than peel thin-skinned tuber crops like potatoes before cooking?
Which fat-soluble vitamin precursor gives orange root crops like carrots and sweet potatoes their vibrant pigment?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most vegetable seeds germinate best in warm darkness because they rely on stored endosperm food until their leaves reach light.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: All vegetable seeds require bright direct sunlight on a sunny windowsill to trigger initial radicle emergence.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Float tests are unreliable because many viable thin or winged seeds naturally trap air, while waterlogged dead seeds can sink.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Seeds that float to the top of a glass of water are guaranteed to be dead, while all sinking seeds will sprout.

extra_misconceptions.fact: High heat and humidity accelerate seed respiration and fungal mold; seeds stay viable longest in cool, dry, airtight containers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Storing leftover seed packets in a hot, humid garden shed preserves embryo viability until the next planting season.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Seed lots with moderate viability can still produce healthy crops if you sow them at twice the normal density and thin as needed.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A seed lot with a 50 percent germination rate must be thrown away because none of its seedlings will grow vigorously.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it important to test exactly 100 randomly selected seeds rather than cherry-picking only the plumpest ones?
What happens to dormant seeds inside a sealed germination bag if the paper towel is dripping wet with standing water?
Which embryonic plant part emerges first from a viable seed coat to confirm that germination has truly begun?
What adjustment should a Scout make to garden row spacing if a viability test shows only 60 percent germination?

extra_misconceptions.fact: An arboretum is a living museum dedicated to researching, conserving, and displaying woody trees and shrubs for public education.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An arboretum and a commercial retail nursery serve the exact same scientific mission of selling seasonal bedding plants.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Accurate soil tests require mixing multiple core samples taken from 6 inches deep across the entire planting area into a composite.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A single scoop of soil taken from one corner of a garden bed gives a county extension lab an accurate nutrient profile.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Land-grant university extension offices provide local homeowners and Scouts with soil testing, pest diagnostics, and planting guides.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: County cooperative extension offices only advise multi-acre commercial farms and do not assist backyard gardeners.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Glass conservatories maintain controlled tropical or arid microclimates for plants that would freeze outdoors in local USDA zones.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Any thriving perennial displayed inside a botanical garden conservatory will survive outdoors in the local winter zone.

extra_socratic_questions: What soil sampling procedure must you follow in your garden before bringing a sample to a county extension office?
Which scientific naming convention on botanical garden plaques avoids confusion caused by regional common plant names?
Where should a nursery quarantine newly delivered plant stock to prevent introducing pests into production greenhouses?
What environmental parameters inside a commercial greenhouse are regulated to harden or force seasonal plant growth?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Wind pollinates staple grasses like wheat, corn, and rice, whereas insects pollinate nutrient-dense fruits, nuts, and vegetables.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cereal grains like wheat, corn, and rice depend on honeybee visits to set seed and would vanish without insect pollinators.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Bees gather protein-rich pollen and sugary nectar to feed their colony brood, transferring pollen between flower stigmas by accident.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Worker honeybees intentionally collect pollen grains just to fertilize the flowers they visit for the gardener.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Vascular tissues transport systemic insecticides throughout the entire plant, exposing foraging bees to neurotoxins in nectar.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Systemic neonicotinoid pesticides applied to soil stay locked in plant roots and never reach flower nectar or pollen.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Monoculture fields bloom for only a few weeks, leaving bees with a nutritional desert unless diverse wildflowers bloom nearby.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Large single-crop agricultural monocultures provide year-round balanced nutrition for resident honeybee colonies.

extra_socratic_questions: Which behavioral trait makes honeybees called floral-constant during a single foraging trip across an orchard?
Why is it dangerous to honeybees when a gardener sprays broad-spectrum insecticides on open blossoms during midday?
What happens to the shape and seed development of a cucumber or squash if its female flower receives too little pollen?
Which parasitic mite feeds on developing honeybee pupae inside capped brood cells and transmits debilitating viruses?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Many garden insects, including alligator-shaped ladybug larvae and hoverfly maggots, are beneficial predators that devour aphids.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every beetle or insect larva spotted on a vegetable leaf is a destructive pest that should be crushed immediately.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Standard Bt (kurstaki) must be eaten by actively feeding caterpillars to work and has no effect on aphids, beetles, or spider mites.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Spraying bacterial Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) kills sap-sucking aphids, spider mites, and adult squash bugs on contact.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Applying soaps or horticultural oils above 85 degrees Fahrenheit or in direct sun causes severe leaf scorch (phytotoxicity).
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Organic insecticidal soap and neem oil cannot burn plant leaves even when sprayed in hot midday summer sunlight.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cold home compost piles rarely get hot enough to kill fungal spores, so diseased vines must be bagged and removed from the garden.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Composting tomato vines infected with late blight or wilt fungi in a cold backyard pile sterilizes the plant pathogens.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it critical to distinguish chewing damage from piercing-sucking damage before choosing an organic pest control?
What happens to beneficial ladybugs and lacewings when you spray a non-selective synthetic pyrethroid across a garden?
Under what condition does splashing irrigation water onto lower tomato leaves trigger an outbreak of early blight?
Where should a Scout inspect host plants to locate camouflaged tomato hornworms or clusters of squash bug eggs?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Vermicomposting requires surface-dwelling epigeic worms like Eisenia fetida (red wigglers), as soil-burrowing nightcrawlers die in bins.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Deep-burrowing earthworms dug up from backyard lawn soil thrive inside shallow indoor vermicompost bins.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Meat, dairy, and pet feces attract scavenging rodents, create putrid odors, and harbor human pathogens that survive home composting.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Adding meat scraps, dairy products, and pet waste to a backyard compost bin speeds up healthy microbial breakdown.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Submerged roots suffocate and develop Pythium root rot unless an air stone or air gap supplies dissolved oxygen to the root zone.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Plant roots submerged in a stationary bucket of hydroponic water absorb plenty of oxygen directly from the water molecules.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Thermophilic composting microbes require continuous oxygen flow from vents and regular turning to prevent foul anaerobic fermentation.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Sealing a compost bin completely airtight traps heat and accelerates the aerobic bacteria that break down yard waste.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a 90-day outdoor compost pile if you load it with wet green grass clippings and no dry brown leaves?
Which physical indicator or smell warns you that a vermicompost worm bin has gone anaerobic from overfeeding?
What measurement confirms that your hydroponic nutrient solution has the proper acidity for plant roots to absorb iron?
Why is it dangerous to red wiggler worms if a vermicompost bin reaches the 140-degree temperatures of hot composting?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Commercial applicators must pass state licensing exams and complete continuing education before handling restricted-use chemicals.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Commercial horticulturists and landscape contractors can legally apply any agricultural pesticide without state certification.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Master Gardener programs train volunteer educators through university extension offices to provide public gardening outreach.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: University Cooperative Extension Master Gardener titles are paid commercial degrees used to bill clients for landscaping.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Horticulture careers span plant pathology, controlled-environment greenhouse management, arboriculture, and seed breeding.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Professional gardening careers are limited to seasonal lawn mowing and offer no laboratory or year-round management paths.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Advanced gardening hobbies involve recurring costs for media, pest monitoring, climate gear, and society memberships.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Specialty gardening hobbies like orchid propagation or beekeeping require no ongoing club dues or equipment budgets after setup.

extra_socratic_questions: What state licensing step must an aspiring commercial nursery manager complete before applying restricted-use pesticides?
Which credential distinguishes a certified arborist or extension Master Gardener from an unlicensed residential landscaper?
What startup expense metrics should your hobby or career log track when comparing greenhouse propagation against open beds?
Why is it dangerous to enter a commercial greenhouse or turf management job without verifying EPA Worker Protection training?
